findings.title: Assertion (i) 'successor stays blocked' is a weak state pin; (f) carries the successor-blocking proof
findings.evidence: Tasks are created with execution_state default 'blocked' (supabase/migrations/20260910055556_engineering_ordered_changes.sql:72), and no predecessor retry or relaunch path changes the successor's state. Under a two-function misclassification that relaunches the failed predecessor (scratchpad/a4r2/v2.tap), assertions 124-128 fail but 'ok 129 - successor of a failed change stays blocked' still passes. The assertion is prescribed by the spec (guidance (i)), and (f) at supabase/tests/engineering_native_ownership.sql:404 is the check that actually catches successor advancement (it fails in v2 with native_slot_occupied).

findings.title: Assertion (b) departs from the spec's literal block shape, but is strictly stronger
findings.evidence: Spec guidance (b) asserts ->>'phase' = 'failed'. The head asserts ->>'failureCode' = 'native_operation_failed' (engineering_native_ownership.sql:396-397, commit 4390110). In record_native_stop, code is null exactly when keep_result is true (20260910104500:567-568), and phase is 'failed' exactly when keep_result is false (:574). So a code of native_operation_failed implies phase 'failed'. N stays 9 and the plan stays 1..129. The change is documented in the PR body and the commit message. (b) is not one of the seven listed acceptance bullets.
